newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister says import fall due to weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister says import fall due to weak demand.

text.p: The fall in Italian imports, shown Tuesday in official figures for November 1996, reflects weak domestic demand, said the Italian Foreign Trade minister Augusto Fantozzi in a statement.

Official statistics body ISTAT reported that in November 1996, Italy registered a trade surplus of 4.7 trillion lire with non-European Union nation, as imports fell to 10.532 trillion lire from 11.343 trillion lire in October.

ISTAT added that Italy increased its trade surplus with EU nations in October to 1.700 trillion lire from 1.251 trillion lire in Septmebr 1996. Overall, Italy had a global trade surplus in October of 7.628 trillion lire with imports down 3.6 percent.

"The improvement of the balance contributes in measure to the fall in imports, which reflects the phase of weakness in internal demand within Italy and benefits from the stronger lira which contains the price of imported products," he said.

The note underlined that the fall in Italian exports -- in November with non-EU nations to 15.238 trillion lire from 17.282 trillion lire -- was probably one of the first effects of the loss of competitiveness from the rise in the value of the lira.
